text:
The Panthers look like the Panthers again. They're 7-3 over their last ten, 9-5-2 overall, and they've taken 55% of the five-on-five expected goals, a share that tends to win a lot of hockey games over a season. The goals have roughly matched the chances, so nothing about this looks borrowed.

The top line is a family affair with a hammer in the middle. Sam Bennett between Matthew and Brady Tkachuk has 61% of the chances and 64% of the shot attempts. Carter Verhaeghe with Sam Reinhart and Sandis Vilmanis has been even sharper in a smaller sample: 4.12 expected goals per hour, 68% of the chances. A few players are scoring faster than their chances support, though. Brady Tkachuk and Seth Jones each have 16 points in ten games on about 8.8 expected, and Verhaeghe has 13 on 7.5. Enjoy it, but don't bank it.

Florida lives on special teams, taking 5.25 minors a game and drawing 5.56. The power play makes 1.14 expected goals a game, which turns that chaos into an edge.

The thing to watch is Anton Lundell, day-to-day with an undisclosed injury per Daily Faceoff. His line with Eetu Luostarinen and Vilmanis has allowed just 1.44 expected goals per hour. Our numbers have Florida at 60% for the playoffs in a crowded Atlantic.
headline: Florida is back to bossing games
